t.E640.agn: In 2004 JECFA evaluated glycine as a flavouring substance and concluded that there is no safety concern at current levels of intake.
t.E640.eval: A flavour modifier; an amino acid (glycine), a natural building block of proteins, and its sodium salt. The amount taken in from foods is far greater than that from the additive. In 2004 JECFA concluded that there is no safety concern at current levels of intake.
t.E640.found.1: Processed foods in which Group I additives are generally authorised
t.E640.prod: Produced chemically by reacting chloroacetic acid with ammonia, or separated from the hydrolysis of proteins such as gelatine.
t.E640.regx.0: As a flavouring substance: no safety concern at current levels of intake.
t.E640.regx.1: Group I additive (quantum satis); also authorised at quantum satis in liquid table-top sweeteners.
t.E640.summary: Glycine, the simplest amino acid, and its salt. Gives a slightly sweet taste and is a flavour enhancer.
t.E640.what: An amino acid (glycine) and its sodium salt, used to modify flavour and in sweetener preparations. Glycine is a natural building block of proteins; the amount taken in from foods is much greater than that taken in as an additive.
